output.reason: I find the brief convincing, mainly because early-action yield fell almost as much as regular-decision yield even though early-action decisions weren't delayed. The catch is that the tiers whose awards were cut are also the tiers slowed by merit review, and the brief admits its tier data doesn't split early action from regular decision, so that overlap isn't fully ruled out.
